# User needs: __APP__ (prototype name, or app-wide)

Per prototype (phase 1, `docs/discovery/<prototype>/needs.md`, IDs N-<prototype>-01): derived from its requirements and records, plus needs it missed. App-wide (phase 2, `docs/needs.md`, IDs N-01): the needs of every prototype, rejected ones included, merged.

Format: `N-01: [Who] needs [something].` In plain, everyday words, as you would say it about a person (e.g. "Teachers need information on how their students are doing."). A short "so that …" is optional.

A need is a general need of a stakeholder, independent of any solution: not a feature or a functional requirement, and without the app's own terms. It should still hold if the app were built completely differently. Limits of the owner (budget, time) are constraints, not needs.

Needs are facts: never edited or deleted. One that turns out wrong is marked **withdrawn**, with the reason.

- **Source:** the requirements (PR-…) or per-prototype needs (N-p1-…) it came from, or where it was found (missed-needs checklist item, one of the four worlds, a rejected feature, a dead end).
- **Shapes:** the combined requirements (RQ-…) and, later, the spec requirements (FR-…) it shapes.

| ID | Need | Source | Shapes | Status (active / withdrawn: reason) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| N-01 | | | | active |

## Missed-needs checklist

Checked for: accounts · privacy · errors and failures · offline · accessibility · onboarding · data export · deletion
